title: Red Chilaquiles with Fried Eggs, Crema and Lime Onions
summary: Tortilla chips coated in a sauce of burst tomatoes, toasted ancho and garlic, topped with fried eggs, crema, lime-pickled red onion and coriander.
equipment: large non-stick frying pan with a lid

ingredients.item: small red onion, thinly sliced into rings
small serrano or jalapeño chilli, chopped (optional)
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
soured cream, thinned with 2 tbsp water

steps.title: Pickle the onion
steps.text: Toss half the onion rings with the lime juice and a pinch of the salt and set aside; chop the rest. A few minutes in lime softens their bite and turns them bright pink.

steps.title: Toast the chilli
steps.text: Heat the dry heavy pan over medium-high heat and toast the ancho and garlic, turning, for about 5 min until the chilli is pliable and the garlic is spotted brown. Stem and seed the chilli and peel the garlic. Dry-toasting brings out the chilli's smoky, fruity flavour.

steps.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps.text: Heat the oil in the same pan, add the chopped onion and cook for about 4 min until starting to brown. Add the tomatoes and cook for 5-8 min until they burst, then add the water and simmer for 5-8 min until they have melted down.

steps.title: Blend the sauce
steps.text: Blend the tomato mixture with the ancho, garlic, cumin, chilli, salt and pepper until almost smooth. Return to the pan and simmer for about 5 min until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Heat the oil in the non-stick pan over medium heat, crack in the eggs and season. Cook for 2 min until the whites are crisp at the edges, then add 1 tbsp water, cover and cook for 2-3 min until the whites and yolks are fully set (71 °C). The steam under the lid sets the top without the base burning.

steps.title: Coat the chips
steps.text: Stir the chips into the hot sauce in two batches until coated, then take off the heat. They should soften at the edges but keep some crunch, so work quickly.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide among plates, top each with a fried egg, drizzle with the crema and scatter over the lime onions and coriander. Serve straight away.

tips: The usual mistake is letting the chips sit in the sauce, which turns them to mush; coat them just before serving.
Use thick, sturdy chips; thin ones collapse in the sauce.
Taste the sauce before adding salt: salty chips add more as they soak.
Add sliced avocado or radishes for freshness.
storage: Best eaten at once. The sauce keeps refrigerated up to 4 days or frozen up to 3 months; reheat until simmering (74 °C) before adding fresh chips. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
